candidates.angle: user topic: same MathML as master
candidates.summary: GetNextToken now hands back as a plain token a } that \left or \bigl turned into an opener, so \sideset reads scripts that master dropped. This breaks the PR's claim that every expression master converts without error converts to the same MathML
candidates.failure_scenario: \sideset{\left}^a}}{}x (or \bigl} in place of \left}) converts without error on both sides. Master draws <none></none> in the last prescript slot. The branch draws <mi>a</mi>. Master's GetNextToken answered ErrTokenBufferExpr for any unescaped curly opener, and cmd_sideset's getScripts stopped there. matched() requires Value "{", so the folded } now comes back as a token and the ^a after it is read. The input is malformed (\left} is not a valid delimiter) and nothing valid changes. A reader loses only the PR body's universal claim (TLDR: 'Every expression master converts without error converts to the same MathML'), which needs scoping to valid TeX or to the corpus.
candidates.verify_by: Copy tests/solo-finder-sideset-curly-fence.go into the mathml package with the master package copied to zzbase, as its header says, then run go test -count=1 -run TestZZSideset -v: expect FAIL, master <none></none> against branch <mi>a</mi>
candidates.evidence: \sideset{\left}^a}}{}x same=false; base err=<nil> ...<mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><none></none></mmultiscripts>; head err=<nil> ...<mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mi>a</mi></mmultiscripts>. Also differs for \bigl}. 5.4M grammar expressions (seeds 1,2,3,5,6,7,11,12) and 4.4M go-fuzz execs found no other differing shape: TestZZGram seed 11 n=800000 diffs=0, seed 12 n=800000 diffs=0 with curly fence delimiters left out; FuzzZZ 4,439,246 execs PASS, filtering only the \left}/\bigl} shape.

dropped.summary: colorArgMissing answers differently from the old GetOptions/GetNextExpr on the sliced cell. The cases are a [ closing at or past cellEnd, and a { closing past the cell
dropped.settled_by: By reading: checkGroupNesting unpairs any [ ] that straddles a group, and cellEnd steps over whole groups, so a { reached before cellEnd closes before it. A [ whose closer is at index n falls on the merror path both ways. The fuzzer agrees: TestZZGram over \color, \color[RGB], \color{red} and \color[RGB]{1,2,3} found diffs=0 outside the \left} shape.
